title: Affine full faithfulness for a perfect complex over a filtered colimit
statement: Let (A_i)_{i in I} be a filtered system of rings with colimit A, and let A_0 be one stage. Let E_0 and K_0 be bounded complexes of finite projective A_0-modules. Put E_i=E_0 tensor_{A_0} A_i, K_i=K_0 tensor_{A_0} A_i, E=E_0 tensor_{A_0} A, and K=K_0 tensor_{A_0} A. Then the canonical map $\operatorname{colim}_{i \ge 0} \operatorname{Hom}_{D(A_i)}(E_i,K_i) \to \operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(E,K)$ is an isomorphism. Here $D(-)$ is the notion used in [def-pc-derived-category], and bounded finite-projective complexes are the affine form of [def-pc-perfect-complex].

proof.text: Scalar extension preserves projectivity by the extension/restriction adjunction and preserves zero terms. Thus every extended E₀ is bounded above and projective. Apply [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative], Mathlib IsKProjective.Qh_map_bijective, to represent derived maps by chain maps and detect equality by homotopies. The private helpers prove these facts directly using the quotient comparison natural isomorphism.
Descend a chain map through finite-presentation component data and descend a homotopy relation at a later stage. These are the two finite-data affine statements in the accompanying modules.
Use the transition and canonical equations to identify the resulting map with the given colimit comparison, proving surjectivity and injectivity.
